function: Learned joint control of UAV movement and excitation current weights (collaborative beamforming) to maximize rate to a mobile ground user and minimize flight energy (pp. 7, 9)
system: 8 or 16 UAVs (0.1 W each) form a virtual array to a mobile ground user; interfering BS; Rician fading; 2.4 GHz; no RIS (pp. 4-6, 13)
method: EMOPPO-VLH: evolutionary multi-objective PPO reinforcement learning with LSTM actor-critic and hyper-sphere task selection; trained centrally in simulation, outputs a Pareto set of policies (pp. 9-13)
data_channel: No dataset; custom simulator: Rician small-scale fading with distance path loss (exponent 2), Gauss-Markov user mobility, UAV energy model; no 3GPP model (pp. 5-6, 13)
test_conditions: Trained and tested in one simulated environment; separate scenarios with 8 and 16 UAVs; robustness analyses only in a supplement absent from the PDF (pp. 13, 16)
baselines: Non-learned: MOEA/D and MOPSO (evolutionary multi-objective optimizers). Learned: EDDPG, ETD3, EPPO, EPPO with GRU (evolutionary multi-objective RL variants) (pp. 14-15)
metrics: Total achievable rate f1 (bps), total UAV flight energy f2 (J), inverted generational distance (IGD) and hypervolume (HV) of the Pareto set (pp. 14-15)
complexity: Order of complexity O(Gmax*n*nevo*(sum of layer-size products + M)) for EMOPPO-VLH; O(G*N^2) for MOEA/D and MOPSO; details in a supplement absent from the PDF (pp. 13-14)
q1_support: p. 5: "fading, modeled as a Rician distribution". p. 13: "proposed method interacts with a simulation environment constructed by using mathematical models, rather than relying on pre-collected real-world data". Custom analytical model; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured data.
q2_support: p. 13: "The purpose of setting different scenario scales is to verify the scalability and robustness of our proposed algorithm under varying environmental sizes"; p. 13: "the administrator may train the DRL algorithm for several versions with various numbers of UAVs in advance". Each scale is its own training; no trained model is tested on an unseen condition in the main text.
q3_support: p. 14: "we implement several types of comparison algorithms, including two multi-objective evolutionary algorithms (MOEAs)"; p. 14: "two multi-policy MORLs, namely, evolutionary deep deterministic policy gradient (EDDPG) and evolutionary twin delayed DDPG (ETD3)". Compared on rate f1, energy f2, IGD and HV (Figs. 5-8, pp. 15-16); EPPO variants are not counted.
q4_support: p. 13: "The total complexity of the proposed EMOPPO-VLH is" given as O(Gmax * n * nevo * (sum of layer-size products + M)); p. 14 gives O(G x N^2) for MOEA/D and MOPSO. The detailed analysis (Appendix A.2) is in a supplement absent from the PDF.
q5_support: p. 13: "constructed by using mathematical models, rather than relying on pre-collected real-world data". Custom simulation; no link to code or data appears in the PDF, and no public channel dataset is used.
notes: PDF is arXiv v1 (9 Feb 2025, p. 1) of the TMC paper; the DOI is not printed in the file, but title and authors match. The text layer of p. 15 is garbled (stacked layers), so p. 15 was read from the page image (Figs. 5-7 and Sec. 6.4: EMOPPO-VLH gives the best f1, f2, IGD and HV). Area 6: the DRL agent controls beam weights and movement of a UAV-swarm aerial link; movement is above the physical layer but is learned jointly with the beam weights (p. 9, action space), so the above_phy rule lets it pass. ris=0: RIS appears only in a reference title (p. 17). The supplemental Appendices A-D (complexity details, metrics, robustness and scalability results) are not in the PDF; q2 and q5 were judged on the main text only and the reviewer may want to check the supplement. q3: EPPO and EPPO with GRU are variants of the proposed method and do not count; EDDPG and ETD3 count as standard learners on the same problem.
